title: DuckDB read-only execution reads local files and remote URLs
attacker_source: SQL written by the AI model (steerable by an MCP agent's question or by text in the data) or a widget template from an imported bundle
sink_or_broken_control: DuckDB table functions (read_text, read_blob, read_csv, query, httpfs readers) and quoted-path replacement scans run inside BEGIN TRANSACTION READ ONLY
impact: confidentiality: any file the user can read, including ~/.config/conch/.key and connections.json (all stored DB credentials)
plausibility: guard has no rule for table functions; READ ONLY only blocks writes to the database
closest_control: assertReadOnly + read-only transaction; neither restricts file/network table functions

title: T-SQL batches bypass the single-statement guard
attacker_source: AI-written SQL or an imported widget template on an MSSQL connection
sink_or_broken_control: single-statement check relies on ';'; T-SQL runs semicolon-free batches; MSSQL read-only is a rolled-back transaction
impact: server-side effects outside the rollback (SHUTDOWN, external reads through OPENROWSET/OPENQUERY, long WAITFOR); transactional writes are rolled back
closest_control: forbidden-word list and the MSSQL rollback wrapper

title: openExternal RPC opens any URL
attacker_source: none found: no renderer caller and no XSS sink
impact: would open file:// or custom schemes if reachable

title: Chart style block built with dangerouslySetInnerHTML
closest_control: config keys are synthetic s0..sN and colors come from seriesColor; labels are not interpolated

title: MCP client cap can be exceeded by concurrent handshakes
attacker_source: same-user local process holding the token
sink_or_broken_control: sessions.size checked before the async accept
